title: A Scalable Training-Free Diffusion Model for Uncertainty Quantification
problem: Existing uncertainty quantification methods using generative models require complicated training processes that hinder real-world applications, especially in dynamic UQ tasks where target probability distributions evolve rapidly over time. The challenge is enabling high-dimensional sampling without expensive score function training.
motivation: Generative models can sample from complex high-dimensional probability distributions for uncertainty quantification, which is critical for applications like weather prediction where distributions change dynamically.
method: The approach uses a score-based diffusion model (a generative model that learns gradients pointing toward likely data) without requiring expensive upfront training. Instead, it solves the backward stochastic differential equation (BSDE, a mathematical equation describing how to generate samples) using a parallel-in-time method that distributes computation across multiple time steps simultaneously on multiple GPUs and nodes. Because training is eliminated, the method immediately adapts to changes in the target probability distribution without retraining.
key_novelty: The core idea is using parallel-in-time distributed computation across multiple GPUs to enable a training-free score-based diffusion model that adapts immediately to changing probability distributions.
contributions: Scalable training-free score-based diffusion model for high-dimensional uncertainty quantification
Integration of parallel-in-time methods with diffusion models to solve BSDEs across distributed GPUs
Distributed matrix computation strategy for score estimation across multi-node GPU clusters
Demonstrated strong and weak scaling on Frontier supercomputer with application to hurricane prediction

metrics.speedup: strong and weak scaling on Frontier supercomputer

limitations: Specific computational complexity comparisons and detailed baseline comparisons not discussed in abstract
